text:
sam: heads-up — reproduced a case where aggressive prefetching causes transient degraded reads for small-tenant workloads. timeline: canary roll -> prefetch kicks -> KV pool backs up -> latency spike for unrelated tenants. anyone seen this in prod?
noor: ugh. saw a blip last week, thought it was networking. good find. any reproducible steps?
diego: steps I used: spin up two tenants, one with long seq lengths (streaming), start prefetch=on for that model, then hammer small-req tenant with 20 rps. latency climbs after ~30s.
maya: question: is this about eviction pressure or queueing inside our prefix fetch worker?
sam: looks like both. eviction gets delayed because prefetch entries hold slabs; plus the worker threads queue. we hit a soft-degrade where reads return stale prefix pointers for a handful of keys.
noor: can we short-circuit prefetch when memory pressure crosses threshold? admission control token bucket?
diego: +1. propose two knobs: 1) global prefetch admission (tokens per-second) 2) tenant-weighted priority. we need to avoid starvation.
maya: need to be careful about correctness for read-after-write. if we abort prefetch mid-flight for a tenant that wrote recently, we can't return stale cached prefix. must ensure write path bumps a lease or invalidates prefetched pointer.
linda: fwiw, current handshake: owner sets lease and writes KV, prefetch uses owner metadata to fetch. race if prefetch started before lease write committed. we should gate prefetch on commit flag.
sam: idea: a prefetch admission check that is 'write-protect-aware' — if recent writes on that key < 2s, always allow prefetch to finish, else it's best-effort. but that could be gamed.
noor: alternative: track dependency bit on cache entries: "fresh" vs "best-effort". Best-effort can be evicted anytime; fresh must survive until commit ack. downside: more metadata and cleanup logic.
diego: here's a tiny pseudocode for token bucket + dependency scoring:
```
if global_tokens <= 0: drop_prefetch()
score = tenant_weight / (1 + recent_write_count)
if score < threshold: mark_best_effort(entry)
else: mark_fresh(entry)
```
maya: love that. also add time-decay to recent_write_count so spikes don't permanently penalize.
infra-bot: deploy queued: prefetch-rate-limiter v0.1 pushed to staging by diego at 2026-02-12T09:14Z :rocket:
sam: callbacks: need tests for read-after-write with aborted prefetches, plus eviction correctness when handing off prefix ownership between workers.
linda: edgecase: handoff during eviction — worker A evicts but worker B still has in-flight prefetch. we need an atomic handoff or a tombstone marker so prefetch fails fast.
diego: agree. propose a two-phase handoff: 1) announce intent (tombstone) 2) wait for inflight count to drop or force-cancel prefetches 3) transfer ownership. cheap but adds latency on handoff.
noor: maybe use versioned ownership token: prefetch includes owner_version, on completion it validates owner_version still matches, else discard. simpler and cheaper.
maya: but we must ensure no read path can return a prefix that belonged to an old owner if that owner already evicted — read path should always validate owner_version too.
sam: ok action items: (1) diego add token-bucket admission + tenant weight + version check prototype, (2) maya & linda write read-after-write correctness tests and handoff tombstone stress tests, (3) noor draft perf experiment plan to measure fairness under mixed workloads. I'll coordinate canary.
diego: will send PR with perf numbers and patch notes.
noor: perf plan: baseline, prefetch-unlimited, token-bucket tuned at 5k tokens/s, tenant-weights ratio 10:1, run 30m. collect p95/p99 and evictions/sec.
sam: perfect. let's meet Thurs 10am to review staging results. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
maya: noted. added tests to the rollout checklist.
linda: added tombstone design doc link: https://internal.redwood/notes/prefetch-tombstone (WIP)
infra-bot: reminder: please tag your PRs with "prefetch-admctl" for easier tracking.
